title: wt refs restore <runId> --dry-run --json
description: What `wt refs restore <runId>` would put back. Printed by `wt refs restore <runId> --json` without --yes as the only thing on stdout; it changes nothing. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

runId.description: The run id as given; one not in wt's format is an error.

token.description: Names the plan: pass it to --yes --expect. Null when nothing could be restored, or on error.

id.description: refs/heads/<name> or refs/tags/<name> here; origin:refs/heads/<name> or origin:refs/tags/<name> on origin. --only takes it, one id per flag and never split: a ref name may contain a comma.

action.description: create: the name is free; it is made at object. none: it is already there at object; only the pin goes. occupied: the name holds another object here. remoteOccupied: origin has something there. endpointChanged: a remote ref, and origin no longer resolves to the URLs the run recorded in its meta. endpointUnknown: a remote ref, and the run has no meta. pinGone: the pin is not there any more; a pin that goes between the plan and the run is reported as kept, its reason starting pinGone.

selected.description: A restore with this plan acts on it: every row whose action is create or none, or what --only names.
